note: Very long periodic sentence with a hard clause left in Shakespeare's shape; split it.
replacement: PAULINA. Good my liege, I come, and I beg you to hear me. I profess myself your loyal servant, your physician, your most obedient counselor. Yet I dare show it less, in comforting your sufferings, than those who seem most to be yours. I say I come from your good queen.

note: "Unvenerable" and "forced baseness" are left untranslated and opaque to a modern reader.
replacement: PAULINA. May your hands be forever unworthy of respect if you pick up the princess under that forced disgrace of bastardy which he has put upon her!

note: Source pairs death with not doing it and reward with its being done; "both for" muddles this.
replacement: Apollo, pardon my great profaneness against your oracle! I'll reconcile myself to Polixenes, woo my queen anew, and recall the good Camillo, whom I proclaim a man of truth and mercy. For, being carried away by my jealousies to bloody thoughts and revenge, I chose Camillo as the agent to poison my friend Polixenes. That would have been done, except that the good mind of Camillo delayed my swift command, though I threatened him with death if he did not do it and encouraged him with reward if it was done. He, most humane and full of honor, unfolded my plot to my kingly guest, gave up his fortunes here, which you knew were great, and committed himself to the certain hazard of all uncertainties, no richer than his honor. How he glitters through my rust! And how his piety makes my deeds the blacker!

note: "fancies" reads as a verb with no object-producing verb, and the prince sentence is very long; add the verb and split.
replacement: PAULINA. What studied torments, tyrant, do you have for me? What wheels? Racks? Fires? What flaying? Boiling in lead or oils? What old or newer torture must I receive, I whose every word deserves to taste your very worst? Your tyranny, working together with your jealousies, has produced fancies too weak for boys, too green and idle for girls of nine. Oh, think what they have done, and then run mad indeed, stark mad! For all your past foolishness was only spice to it. That you betrayed Polixenes was nothing. That only showed you to be, of a fool, inconstant and damnably ungrateful. Nor was it much that you would have poisoned good Camillo's honor, by having him kill a king. These are poor trespasses, when a more monstrous one stands beside them. Of those I reckon the casting out of your baby daughter to the crows to be little or nothing, though a devil would have shed water out of fire before doing it. Nor is it directly laid to you that the young prince is dead. His honorable thoughts, thoughts too high for one so tender, split the heart that could conceive that a gross and foolish father had blemished his gracious mother. This is not, no, laid to your account. But the last, oh lords, when I have said it, cry Woe! The queen, the queen, the sweetest, dearest creature, is dead, and vengeance for it has not dropped down yet.

note: "If ever you have spent time worse than now, then do" misreads "ere now" and is garbled.
replacement: TIME. I who please some and test everyone, who bring both joy and terror to good and bad, who make errors and unfold them, now take it on myself, in the name of Time, to use my wings. Don't count it a crime in me or in my swift passage that I slide over sixteen years and leave unexamined the growth in that wide gap. It is in my power to overthrow law, and in a single self-born hour to plant new custom and overwhelm the old. Let me pass the same as I am, as I was before the most ancient order existed, and before what is accepted now. I witnessed the times that brought those things in, and I shall do the same to the freshest things now reigning. I will make the glitter of this present age grow stale, just as my tale now seems stale to it. If you allow me your patience, I turn my hourglass, and give my scene such growth as if you had slept through the gap between. Leontes has been left with the effects of his foolish jealousies, and grieves so much that he shuts himself away. Imagine me, gentle spectators, now to be in fair Bohemia, and remember well that I mentioned a son of the king's, whom I now name to you as Florizel. I move on quickly to speak of Perdita, now grown in grace to equal the wonder she causes. What follows for her I don't care to prophesy, but let Time's news be known when it is brought forth. A shepherd's daughter, and whatever attaches to her, and whatever follows after, is the subject of Time's tale. Accept this, if you have ever spent time worse before now. If never, still Time himself says he earnestly hopes you never will.
